subject: Proposal: tiered token ladder + EU rounding flow
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@retaillytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question on token bands and EU invoice rounding

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look promising. Before we move to a formal PO we need clarity on two items so Finance can sign off: 1) How our committed monthly tokens map to discount bands (we'd like to understand mid-month bursts and how those are billed), and 2) how Redwood handles rounding on EU invoices once VAT and EUR conversion are applied (our local accounting requires invoice line-level rounding to 2 decimals which has tripped us up in other vendors).

Specifically: if we commit to 8M tokens / month with a 15% discount band, and we spike an extra 1.2M tokens mid-cycle, are the extra tokens billed at list or at the committed band? Also, do you round per-line or at the invoice total after VAT?

Attached a sample invoice from another vendor so you can see the mismatch that caused us to chase credits last quarter. Appreciate a clear worked example we can share with our FP&A.

Best,
Maya
Procurement, Retaillytics

Attachment: sample-vendor-invoice.pdf (pdf, 240KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@retaillytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on token bands and EU invoice rounding

Hi Maya — really glad Retaillytics liked the demo. Short answer up front: we try to bill extra usage at the committed band's unit price up to a tolerance, and for EU invoices we can publish line-level rounding rules so your AP team gets a predictable number. Below is a concise worked example; I'll loop in Ben and Karthik to confirm accounting mechanics and the contract language.

Worked example (commit = 8,000,000 tokens / mo, committed price = €0.000016/token after 15% discount):
- Normal month usage: 7.9M -> billed at committed price -> invoice line: "Committed usage" 7,900,000 x €0.000016 = €126.40
- Burst: additional 1.2M tokens mid-month -> first 100k of burst absorbed into an intra-month tolerance window (we have a 100k buffer; see contract clause), remaining 1.1M charged at same committed unit price up to a daily cap. If you exceed the monthly committed by >20%, the overflow is billed at list price for the excess.

Rounding / VAT flow for EU: we generate per-line extended amounts with VAT applied per line (so AP sees line-level VAT), then round each line to 2 decimals before summing to invoice total. We can sign the invoice appendix that specifies this rounding policy.

I'll attach a spreadsheet with a few permutations (commit sizes, buffer, overflow thresholds). If acceptable, we can bake the tolerance and overflow rates into the SOW and create a short addendum for EU rounding.

Next steps: Ben / Karthik, can you confirm the buffer and >20% overflow rule vs. our standard >10% rule for pilot credits?

Cheers,
Vanessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Vanessa — quick internal note for the thread. We have two moving parts: pricing lane behavior (what unit price applies to overflow) and commercial concession policy (when do we grant a one-off credit). For Retaillytics (enterprise pilot + potential Dedicated footprint) I recommend:
- Buffer = 100k tokens / month (absorbed, not billed)
- Soft overflow up to 20% of committed monthly tokens billed at committed unit price (this simplifies FP&A and is a strong sales gesture)
- Any additional overflow >20% billed at list price but eligible for a one-time discretionary credit request (handled by Finance ops) if they provide rolling 3mo usage history that justifies it.

On rounding: our EU billing pipeline can emit per-line amounts, apply country VAT, then round each line to 2 decimals. There is a minor engineering backlog item to add an explicit "invoice appendix" feature in the Console. For now we can include the appendix as contract language and produce invoices from a script that applies the described rounding. Ops will need the HubSpot deal flag to toggle the script.

Sergio — can you confirm the hubspot tag name you want us to use for invoice-behavior toggle?

Ben
Director, Pricing & Business Ops

Subject: Re: Question on token bands and EU invoice rounding — proposed terms

Hi Maya / Alex — thanks for the patience while we pulled the examples together. Attached is the updated proposal and a CSV with three billing scenarios (normal, +15% burst, +35% burst) showing line-level arithmetic before and after VAT rounding. Summary of the terms we can commit to in an SOW/addendum:

- Commit: 8,000,000 tokens/mo at committed price €0.000016/token (15% band)
- Monthly buffer: first 100,000 tokens of intra-month burst absorbed (no charge)
- Soft overflow: up to +20% of committed monthly tokens billed at committed unit price
- Hard overflow: any usage beyond +20% billed at list price; discretionary one-time credit considered on a case-by-case basis if customer provides 3mo usage history and spike explanation
- EU invoices: line-level VAT application and 2-decimal rounding per line before summation; Redwood to include invoice appendix specifying exact rounding flow

Please review the attached CSV and let us know which scenario you want to bake into the PO so we can produce a contract draft. Happy to set a short call with Karthik and Ben if FP&A wants live walkthrough of the numbers.

Best,
Vanessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
